pages.title: Basic array operations
pages.content:
In the previous module, we learnt about NumPy arrays
- Different datatypes that can be handled in NumPy
- How do we create 1D / 2D / 3D arrays?
- How do we identify specific elements using index and slicing

In this module, we will do Array manipulation i.e. - change the values of elements within NumPy arrays.

Let us begin!

Broadly, there are 3 types of basic arithmetic operations on NumPy arrays
- Element-wise Operations
- Scalar Operations
- Using Built-in Functions for Arithmetic Computations

practiceProblems.title: Element-wise operations
practiceProblems.description:
Element-wise operations in NumPy allow you to perform arithmetic operations on arrays on an element-by-element basis. When you perform an arithmetic operation on two arrays of the same shape, NumPy performs the operation on each corresponding pair of elements.

Consider the following example and the result
```python
a = np.array([1, 2, 3])
b = np.array([4, 5, 6])
print(a + b)      # Output - [5 7 9]
print(a - b)      # Output - [-3 -3 -3]
print(a * b)      # Output - [4 10 18]
print(a / b)      # Output - [0.25 0.4 0.5]
print(b % a)      # Output - [0 1 0]
```
Note that even the modulo(`%`) operator returns the remainder on division element-wise 

### Task
You are given 2 2D arrays in the IDE. \
Perform the following and output the results to the console.
- Multiplication of the 2 arrays
- Result when array 2 is divided by array 1

practiceProblems.title: Scalar operations
practiceProblems.description:
Scalar operations involve performing arithmetic operations between an array and a single scalar value. The scalar value is applied to each element of the array.

```python
a = np.array([1, 2, 3])
result = a + 10       # Output - [11, 12, 13]
result = a - 10       # Output - [-9, -8, -7]
result = a * 10       # Output - [10, 20, 30]
result = a / 10       # Output - [0.1, 0.2, 0.3]
```

### Task

Perform and output the following results
- Multiple the array with 5
- Divide the array by 10

practiceProblems.title: Built-in Functions for Arithmetic Computations
practiceProblems.description:
NumPy provides built-in functions for various arithmetic computations such as sum, difference, product, and quotient of arrays.

Let us use the built-in functions on a single array. Check out some example and syntax below.
```python
a = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])

print(np.sum(a))         # Output - 15
print(np.prod(a))        # Output - 120
print(np.cumsum(a))      # Output - [1 3 6 10 15]
print(np.cumprod(a))     # Output - [1 2 6 24 120]
```
**Note**
- cumsum - Computes the running total of array elements, returning a new array where each element is the sum of the current and all previous elements.
- cumprod - Computes the running product of array elements, returning a new array where each element is the product of the current and all previous elements.


### Task
Let us use the built-in functions on a 2D array to understand the output better.\
Compute and output the sum, product, cumulative sum and cumulative product for the given 2D array.

practiceProblems.title: Combining logical computations
practiceProblems.description:
Logical operations can be combined using parentheses for grouping to form complex logical expressions.

Consider the snippet below:
```python
bool_array1 = np.array([True, False, True, False])
bool_array2 = np.array([False, False, True, True])

combined = np.logical_or(np.logical_and(bool_array1, bool_array2), np.logical_not(bool_array1))
print(combined)       # Output - [False  True  True  True]
```
- `np.logical_and(bool_array1, bool_array2)` performs an element-wise logical AND operation. \
Output of this is `[False, False, True, False]`
- `np.logical_not(bool_array1)` returns the array - `[False, True, False, True]`
- `np.logical_or` of the above 2 arrays will return `[False  True  True  True]`

We have populated a code to show combined logical operations in 2D arrays.\
Check out the output of this code - try and understand the working of the code.

practiceProblems.title: Variance and standard deviation
practiceProblems.description:
The following Variance and Standard deviation functions are used.
```python
data = np.array([1, 1, 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10])

print(np.var(data))      # Output - 10.36
print(np.std(data))    # Output - 3.2186953878862163
```
Remember that
- [Variance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variance): The average of the squared differences from the mean.
- [Standard Deviation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_deviation): The square root of the variance, representing the dispersion of the data.

### Task
You are given a 3D array - go ahead ad output the variance and standard deviation of the 2nd matrix on separate lines. \
Check the sample output below for further clarity.

practiceProblems.title: Percentiles
practiceProblems.description:
You will need to know how the value below which a given percentage of observations fall.

For example
- Below what compensation do 80% of the developers belong?
- Below what height do 75% and 25% of new born infants belong?

This is known as [percentile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Percentile).

```python
data = np.array([1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3])

print(np.percentile(data, 25))
print(np.percentile(data, 50))
print(np.percentile(data, 75))
```

### Task
Output the 25th, 50th and 75the percentile of the given 3D array.

pages.title: String functions in NumPy
pages.content:
Why do we need to do String manipulation during data analysis?

1. Data Cleaning:
- Whitespace Removal: String data often contains leading or trailing spaces that can cause issues in data analysis. Cleaning up these spaces ensures consistency.
- Case Consistency: Ensuring uniform case (all lowercase or uppercase) can help in consistent data matching and comparison.

2. Data Transformation:
- Concatenation: Combining multiple string fields into one can be useful in creating composite keys or merging columns.
- Replacement and Substitution: Correcting typos or replacing certain parts of strings with new values is common in data cleaning.

3. Data Parsing and Extraction:
- Splitting: Breaking down a string into parts (like splitting a full name into first and last names) helps in organising data better.
- Pattern Matching: Extracting specific patterns from strings (like extracting dates or email addresses) is often needed in data preprocessing.

Let us learn some of the basic string functions in NumPy in this topic.

pages.title: String functions summary
pages.content:
NumPy provides a suite of functions for string operations that are vectorized, meaning they operate on entire arrays at once, providing efficient and concise ways to manipulate string data.

1. String Concatenation and Repetition:
- numpy.char.add(): Adds two strings element-wise.
- numpy.char.multiply(): Repeats each string element-wise a given number of times.

2. Case Conversion:
- numpy.char.capitalize(): Capitalizes the first letter of each string element-wise.
- numpy.char.title(): Converts each string element to title case.
- numpy.char.lower(): Converts each string element to lowercase.
- numpy.char.upper(): Converts each string element to uppercase.
- numpy.char.swapcase(): Swaps the case of each string element.

3. String Splitting and Joining:
- numpy.char.split(): Splits each string element in the array.
- numpy.char.splitlines(): Splits each element at line breaks.
- numpy.char.join(): Joins elements in an array of strings using a specified separator.

4. String Searching:
- numpy.char.find(): Returns the lowest index in each string where the substring is found.
- numpy.char.rfind(): Returns the highest index in each string where the substring is found.

5. String Modification:
- numpy.char.strip(): Removes leading and trailing whitespaces from each string element.
- numpy.char.lstrip(): Removes leading whitespaces from each string element.
- numpy.char.rstrip(): Removes trailing whitespaces from each string element.
- numpy.char.replace(): Replaces substrings in each string element.

6. Character Checking:
- numpy.char.isdigit(): Checks if each string element contains only digits.
- numpy.char.isalpha(): Checks if each string element contains only alphabetic characters.
- numpy.char.isnumeric(): Checks if each string element contains only numeric characters.

By understanding and using these functions, you can efficiently manipulate and process string data, which is a common task in data analysis and preprocessing.

practiceProblems.title: Concatenation and repetition
practiceProblems.description:
Some string functions resemble the arithmetic operations that we did in the previous topics.

For example, we can add strings in 2 arrays - this performs an element-wise concatenation.
```python
arr1 = np.array(['Hello', 'Good'])
arr2 = np.array([' World', ' Morning'])
print(np.char.add(arr1, arr2))     # Output - ['Hello World' 'Good Morning']
```
- Notice that **arr2** already had a space in the strings - hence the space is retained during addition

Similarly - `multiply()` can be used to duplicate a string as many times as required.
```python
arr = np.array(['Hello', 'Good'])
print(np.char.multiply(arr, 3))    # Output - ['HelloHelloHello' 'GoodGoodGood']
```

You can capitalize the first letter of each string element-wise - check the example given below.
```python
arr = np.array(['hello', 'good morning'])
print(np.char.capitalize(arr))     # Output -  ['Hello', 'Good morning']
```

practiceProblems.title: String splitting and joining
practiceProblems.description:
We can split space separated strings present inside the array.
```python
arr = np.array(['hello world', 'good morning'])
print(np.char.split(arr))         # Output - [list(['hello', 'world']) list(['good', 'morning'])]
```
- The output is a NumPy array of lists, where each list contains the split parts of the original strings.

Just as we can split space separated strings, we can also split a string based on line separators.
```python
arr = np.array(['hello\nworld', 'good\nmorning\neveryone'])
print(np.char.splitlines(arr))    # Output - [list(['hello', 'world']) list(['good', 'morning', 'everyone'])]
```

We can join elements in an array of strings using a specified separator.
```python
arr = np.array(['hello', 'world'])
separator = '-'
print(np.char.join(separator, arr))      # Output - ['h-e-l-l-o' 'w-o-r-l-d']
```

Go ahead and run the code given in the IDE to see how this functions. \
You can also change the separator to see the change in output.

practiceProblems.description:
`numpy.char.find()` returns the lowest index in each string where the substring is found. If the substring is not found, it returns -1.
```python
arr = np.array(['hello world', 'good morning', 'hello everyone'])

print(np.char.find(arr, substring))        # Output - [ 4  1  4]
```

`numpy.char.rfind()` returns the highest index in each string where the substring is found. If the substring is not found, it returns -1.
```python
arr = np.array(['hello world', 'good morning', 'hello everyone'])
substring = 'o'
print(np.char.rfind(arr, substring))       # Output - [ 7  6 11]
```

practiceProblems.title: String modification
practiceProblems.description:
`numpy.char.strip()` removes leading and trailing whitespaces from each string element in the array. This is useful for cleaning up data where extra spaces might be present around the text.
```python
arr = np.array(['  hello  world ', '  beautiful day  ', ' numpy '])
print(np.char.strip(arr))        # Output - ['hello  world' 'beautiful day' 'numpy']
```
Note: Spaces between strings are not removed. This only removes leading and trailing whitespaces.

`numpy.char.lstrip()` removes leading whitespaces from each string element in the array. This is useful when you need to clean up spaces only from the beginning of the strings. \
Similarly, `numpy.char.rstrip()` removes trailing whitespaces from each string element in the array. This is useful when you need to clean up spaces only from the end of the strings.
```python
arr = np.array(['  hello  world ', '  beautiful day  ', ' numpy '])
print(np.char.lstrip(arr))       # Output - ['hello  world ' 'beautiful day  ' 'numpy ']
print(np.char.rstrip(arr))       # Output - ['  hello  world' '  beautiful day' ' numpy']
```

`numpy.char.replace()` replaces occurrences of a specified substring within each string element of the array with a new substring. This is useful for correcting or modifying text data.
```python
arr = np.array(['hello world', 'goodbye world'])     
print(np.char.replace(arr, 'world', 'universe'))      # Output - ['hello universe' 'goodbye universe']
```

practiceProblems.title: Character checking functions
practiceProblems.description:
`numpy.char.isdigit()` checks if each string element in the array contains only digit characters (0-9). It returns a boolean array of the same shape, where each element is True if the corresponding string contains only digits, and False otherwise.
```python
arr = np.array(['123', '456a', '7890', 'abc', '42'])
print(np.char.isdigit(arr))        # Output - [ True False  True False  True]
```

Similar to the function above, `numpy.char.isalpha()` checks if each string element in the array contains only alphabetic characters (a-z, A-Z). It returns a boolean array of the same shape, where each element is True if the corresponding string contains only alphabetic characters, and False otherwise.
```python
arr = np.array(['abc', 'Hello', 'world123', 'XYZ', '42'])
print(np.char.isalpha(arr))        # Output - [ True  True False  True False]
```

`numpy.char.isnumeric()` checks if each string element in the array contains only numeric characters. Numeric characters include digit characters and characters that represent numbers in other number systems (e.g., fractions, subscripts, superscripts). It returns a boolean array of the same shape, where each element is True if the corresponding string contains only numeric characters, and False otherwise.
```python
arr = np.array(['123', '456a', 'IV', 'abc', '42'])
result = np.char.isnumeric(arr)    # Output - [ True False False False  True]
```
